text:
maya: Pushed a draft Grafana dashboard for per-token tail analysis and KV reuse. Goal is to correlate token-level jitter with eviction spikes and kernel changes. Draft link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/XYZ (draft)
arjun: Nice — what's the main set of queries/panels?
maya: Main panels: 1) token latency p50/p95/p99 by route+kernel 2) kv_cache hit rate by route 3) evictions/sec by model+shard 4) per-shard memory_in_use 5) reuse_ratio = prefix_hits / total_requests by route
lucy: Can you paste the PromQL for p99 so I can hook it into the alert?
maya: ```promql
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_generation_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route, kernel))
```
devon: Caveat: buckets vary across models. Might be safer to derive p99 from a summary metric or compute from quantiles exporter. Also filter out warmup traffic first.
samir: Quick profile note: after the kernel switch last week, p99 increased ~12% on routes with long prefixes and evictions spiked ~3x. Looks like a change in KV access ordering.
maya: I saw that too. Dashboard includes delta_vs_baseline panels that compare kernel:v1 -> kernel:v2 per route so we can spot regressions.
arjun: Can we add a prefetch vs runtime usage panel? e.g., prefetch_reserved_bytes / kv_memory_used per shard — helps see wasted reservation.
maya: Good idea. I'll add a prefetch gauge and an occupancy heatmap: per-shard 2D histogram of prefix_length vs hit_rate.
perf-bot: Alert created: rule=kv_eviction_rate_high, condition=evictions_rate>50 for 5m, ticket=RD-5182
lucy: For reuse_ratio please use a 1s aligner and annotate sample size. Also add a smoothed ratio (EMA) to avoid flapping on low-volume routes.
devon: On instrumentation: we should tag KV metrics with kernel_variant and batching_mode labels so we can attribute changes to kernel selection or batching heuristics.
maya: Agreed. I'll modify the exporter to add labels kernel_variant and batching_mode for all kv_* metrics. Also plan to include an annotated snapshot of a slow request (logs + kv key dump). Example CLI for debug: ```bash
redwood debug get-slow-request --id 0x7f2a --include-kv-keys
```
samir: Do we have capacity for storing kv dumps for 7 days? Retention costs might be high if we dump full shards.
maya: Plan: 1:10 sampled mini-dumps retained 24h, full dumps only on-demand when we escalate. That should keep cost low.
arjun: LGTM. Next steps: maya updates dashboard + PromQL, devon adds exporter labels, samir runs a small A/B rollback test on one shard to validate kernel impact. I'll sync this into the weekly runtime meeting.
maya: Thanks all :thumbsup:
